concepts.label: SQL++ Support for Couchbase Transactions (concept page)

relations.subject: n1ql:begin-transaction
relations.evidence: The `BEGIN TRANSACTION` statement enables you to begin a sequence of statements as an ACID transaction. For more information, see [SQL++ Support for Couchbase Transactions](transactions.md).

relations.subject: n1ql:begin-transaction
relations.evidence: You can also specify a single DML statement as an ACID transaction by setting the [tximplicit](../n1ql-manage/query-settings.md#tximplicit) query parameter.

relations.subject: n1ql:begin-transaction
relations.evidence: To specify transaction settings, see [SET TRANSACTION](set-transaction.md).

relations.subject: n1ql:begin-transaction
relations.evidence: To rollback a transaction, see [ROLLBACK TRANSACTION](rollback-transaction.md).

notable_absence.finding: Unlike the DDL statements in this round (GRANT/REVOKE/CREATE BUCKET etc.), BEGIN TRANSACTION carries no access-control gate at all - no Capella role requirement, no credential-type restriction, no named-role privilege. The only prerequisite content on the page is behavioral (the statement must begin with BEGIN/START and contain WORK/TRAN/TRANSACTION) and routing-related (all statements in a transaction are pinned to the same Query node).

cross_component_finding: The page links out to server/'s transaction overview ('For an overview of Couchbase transactions, see [Transactions](../../../server/current/learn/data/transactions.md)') and to a footnote requiring 'cbq shell version 2.0 or above' for automatic transaction ID handling - both server/-shared, cbq-shell-specific concerns rather than anything Capella-specific. This SQL++ transaction-statement family (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/SAVEPOINT/SET TRANSACTION) reads as shared source content presented unchanged on the Capella docs tree, similar in spirit to (though not an instance of) the server-version-citation anomaly - here it's shared server/ conceptual content and cbq-shell version gating rather than a literal 'Couchbase Server X.Y' string, so not logged against that specific docs-issue.
cross_product_finding: Open question (per task brief): no textual evidence on this page connects SQL++'s BEGIN TRANSACTION to the Java SDK's distributed-transaction feature (sdk:distributed-transaction). The page's only related-links are to other SQL++ transaction statements, the server/ transaction overview, and a Couchbase blog post ('Couchbase Transactions: Elastic, Scalable, and Distributed') - no SDK cross-reference is present, so no relation is asserted. Flagging as open: whether SQL++ transactions (this statement family) and the Java SDK's distributed ACID transactions (sdk:distributed-transaction) are the same underlying server-side transaction mechanism exposed through two different client surfaces is plausible but unconfirmed by any page text seen so far.
